gates.result: The prepare, bind-review, validate, evaluate, and invalidate commands implement a fail-closed offline workflow. Preparation seals exactly 50 waybills and 100 unique images, and only evaluate may construct a qualified local OCR runtime.

Quality scenes bind exact image or waybill-pair subjects to the sealed human truth, review attestations are canonically recomputed, and complete immutable quality and decision records persist through backup and restore.

If a formal result influences an executable artifact or label, permanent invalidation changes the dataset authority. Application and repository replay both reject that stale formal result, including concurrent invalidation boundaries.

Formal evaluation is factory-owned and binds the complete OCR composition evidence hash together with the runtime set, build, template, matcher, and policy identities. Manual backends cannot authorize a formal release.

The authoritative check passed Ruff, mypy for 140 source files, 797 backend tests with two environment-limited skips, 70 frontend tests, boundary verification, lint, typecheck, and production build. No real or legacy system was used.

The release mechanism is implemented, but no independent human-confirmed locked set of exactly 50 unseen waybills and 100 unique ticket images has been supplied or evaluated. Real accuracy and Loop 7 acceptance remain unclaimed.
